title: Tavelo Attack Review - Premium Chinese Goodness

takeaways.text: The geometry is on the short side for an all-rounder; even with a 130 mm stem he would like more reach because of his long arms.
It climbs very well, close to his Giant Propel, which is stiffer and slightly better; it climbs better than his Winspace T1500, though the Winspace is more exciting and harsher.
He recalls his built bike at about 7.1 kg in white paint, and thinks a lighter finish could bring it under 7 kg.
He finds the roughly US$1,600 frameset fair, fairer than the upcoming Arow, but warns that rising Chinese prices and no local dealer support weaken the case against big brands.

He rates it a refined, comfortable all-rounder whose rear end does not get upset by rough pavement, and stable on 40 mph descents; the instability he felt came from the wide front wheel in crosswinds.

disclosure: Panda Podium supplied the frameset; the wheels are also from a supplier he works with.
summary: A follow-up after a few months riding a size-56 Tavelo Attack built with Ultegra Di2 and Craft Racing Works wheels.
